items.finding: Low-level data fusion is regarded as the most straightforward strategy for merging inputs, where variables from distinct sources are placed sequentially into a single data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing whether concatenating rescaled spectral blocks from MIR ATR and fluorescence into a single matrix provides practical gains. The team should evaluate if the added complexity of fusing both modalities actually improves classification over individual methods.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The review notes that instrument complementarity does not guarantee improved predictive performance in all analytical setups. Performance will depend heavily on the specific biological tissue matrix and data synchronization rather than general data fusion principles.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E03 ¶31

items.finding: Prior to combining information from distinct sources, it is crucial to assess how much each individual dataset contributes to the model and verify their complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: The customer should independently validate and benchmark both MIR ATR and fluorescence data to ensure that both provide non-redundant value before proceeding to a fused model. This diagnostic step directly informs whether the combined sensor architecture provides measurable advantage.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited review covers general process analytical technology applications rather than dual-mode fiber-optic spectroscopy on heterogeneous biological tissues. Methodological suitability must be confirmed experimentally for this interface.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
